1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels refer to the manuscript
     6	revision 3920258 and are written exactly as in its LaTeX source (for
     7	example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written and reviewed
     8	at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9 and ba01d98. The later revisions
     9	changed only prose, titles, the literature review, layout and figures:
    10	every cited label exists in all four, and the mathematical expressions of
    11	each cited statement and its proof are the same up to whitespace and braces
    12	(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    13	
    14	## Scope
    15	
    16	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    17	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    18	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    19	  elaborated types.
    20	- The rows cover every public theorem (611) and 113 definitions whose
    21	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other
    22	  49 public definitions (for example
    23	  `kappa`, `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`) only name quantities used in those
    24	  statements and have no rows of their own; read their bodies in the Lean
    25	  source or in `Audit/`.
    26	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    27	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    28	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    29	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    30	- The twenty-six `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    31	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and
    32	  time-fractional foundation of `ClockCopy`, and `GaussianTest` is the
    33	  Gaussian-test foundation of `MaskedSpectralGrowth`) model `H:homog` and
    34	  formalize the conclusions of twenty-three
    35	  labelled results in full. Twenty need no supplied input:
    36	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own
    37	  hypotheses. `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are
    38	  proved under weaker hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no
    39	  `delta < 1`) and also stated exactly as the manuscript does by the
    40	  wrappers `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the
    41	  Rayleigh lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is
    42	  not formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    43	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under

  1365	
  1366	Covers two modules, `TimeSchur` and `MaskedModulation`, on
  1367	`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex` at `3920258` (the file is
  1368	identical at `ba01d98`, so every label and line number below holds at both).
  1369	It formalizes the Schur bound `E:masked-time-schur` (lines 150-152, inside
  1370	`L:masked-time-completion`, lines 141-156) and `L:masked-temporal-modulation`
  1371	(lines 300-309, display `E:masked-temporal-modulation` at 303-307), both in
  1372	double-integral form. It also re-issues `L:masked-trig-products` (lines
  1373	347-374) with one supplied input replaced by a narrower one.
  1374	
  1375	What is stated. The manuscript's left sides are norms in the temporal
  1376	completion `H_a` and its complexification `H_a^C`. The completion is not
  1377	constructed in Lean. On real compact smooth tests, `||f||_a^2` is by
  1378	definition the double integral
  1379	`int_0^T int_0^T f(t) f(s) |t-s|^(-a) dt ds` (lines 143-145). By lines
  1380	153-154 and 177-179, the complexified norm of every `f` in `L^2(0,T)` is the
  1381	same double integral with `f(t) conj f(s)`. Lean bounds exactly these double
  1382	integrals: `TimeSchur.timeForm a T f g` is the iterated integral over
  1383	`[0,T]^2` of `f(t) conj g(s) |t-s|^(-a)`, and `TimeSchur.kern a x = |x|^(-a)`.
  1384	
  1385	`E:masked-time-schur`. `time_schur_paper` covers real `f` in `L^2(0,T)`
  1386	under the hypotheses `0 < a < 1` and `T > 0`. It proves that the integrand is
  1387	integrable on `[0,T]^2` and that the double integral is at most
  1388	`(2T^(1-a)/(1-a)) int f^2`. `time_schur_complex` gives the same bound for
  1389	`|timeForm a T f f|` with complex `f` (the complexified form, lines 175-177).
  1390	The proof is the TeX's: the row integral is at most `2T^(1-a)/(1-a)` (lines
  1391	171-172; Lean computes it exactly in `integral_row`), then
  1392	`2|xy| <= x^2 + y^2` and Tonelli.
  1393	
  1394	`L:masked-temporal-modulation`. `masked_temporal_modulation_paper` takes the
  1395	standing assumptions of lines 296-298 and of `L:masked-time-completion`
  1396	(`T > 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `I = [s, s+h]` inside `[0,T]`, `0 < h <= 1`) and the
  1397	lemma's hypotheses (`A` is `C^1` on `I`, `M = sup_I |A|`, `D = sup_I |A'|`).
  1398	For every real `omega`, with `F = 1_I A e^(i omega t)`, it proves two things:
  1399	the integrand `F(t) conj F(u) |t-u|^(-a)` is integrable on `[0,T]^2`, and
  1400	`|timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1)` with
  1401	`C0(a) = 16/(1-a)`. This bounds the absolute value of the complex double
  1402	integral, which implies the bound on its real part. The constant depends only
  1403	on `a`, which is the stated uniformity in `T, s, h, A, omega` (line 308).
  1404	
  1405	The proof route differs from the TeX's; only the statement and the constant
  1406	`C0(a)` match. The TeX differentiates `c(v)` at the moving endpoint (lines
  1407	312-318), splits the square into two conjugate triangles (lines 318-324),
  1408	treats `|omega h| <= 1` directly (lines 326-329), integrates by parts on
  1409	`[1/k, 1]` for `k = |omega h| > 1`, and closes with `8 sqrt 2 <= 16` (lines
  1410	331-345). Lean proceeds as follows:
  1411	
  1412	- `c` is `acorr Phi v = int_R Phi(u+v) conj Phi(u) du` with `Phi = 1_I A`.
  1413	  For `0 <= v <= h` this is the TeX's `c(v)`; that identification is not
  1414	  itself a Lean statement.
  1415	- No derivative of `c` is used. `acorr_bound` proves `|c(v)| <= M^2 (h-v)_+`,
  1416	  which contains the TeX's `c(h) = 0` and `|c| <= hM^2`. `acorr_lip` proves
  1417	  `|c(v) - c(w)| <= (M^2 + hMD)(w - v)`, the integrated form of the TeX's
  1418	  `|c'| <= M^2 + hMD`.
  1419	- A shear substitution and Fubini (`timeForm_eq_acorr`) give
  1420	  `timeForm = int_R |v|^(-a) e^(i omega v) c(v) dv`. The symmetry
  1421	  `c(-v) = conj c(v)` (`integral_acorr_split`) writes this as `X + conj X`,
  1422	  with `X` the integral over `v > 0`.
  1423	- Case `<h omega> <= 8` (it contains the TeX's case `|omega h| <= 1`):
  1424	  `crude_bound` with `constant_small`.
  1425	- Case `<h omega> > 8`, so `k = h|omega| > 7`: the integration by parts is
  1426	  replaced by a half-period shift `v -> v + pi/|omega|` (`osc_bound`, with
  1427	  the explicit majorant `majorant`). The final check is `4 pi 8/7 <= 16`
  1428	  (`constant_large`).

1529	## MaskedSpectralGrowth (whole result)
  1530	
  1531	Formalizes `P:masked-spectral-growth` (`notes/integrated_covariance_foundation.tex`
  1532	at `3920258`, lines 34-77) in full, with its displays
  1533	`E:masked-gaussian-transform` (lines 42-45) and `E:masked-translated-ball`
  1534	(lines 46-49). It also derives the spectral homogeneity
  1535	`mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A)`, which `SpectralHomog`, `DampedNorms` and
  1536	`ClockCopy` take as their one supplied input. The TeX derives it from the
  1537	scaling of `Gamma` and Fourier uniqueness: proof of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
  1538	in `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `3920258`, lines
  1539	704-705, and proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines 4521-4525. The section covers
  1540	three modules. `GaussianTest` is the foundation (rows marked
  1541	"[foundation: GaussianTest]"): Mathlib has no Gaussian Schwartz map, so the
  1542	module builds `x -> exp(-c norm(x)^2)` (`c > 0`) as one by hand
  1543	(`gaussSchwartz`, decay from the Faa di Bruno bound
  1544	`norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le`). From it, it builds the complex test
  1545	`gaussTest s hs w y`, `x -> e^(-i<y,x>) e^(-s norm(x-w)^2)` (`s > 0`), and
  1546	proves its Fourier integral on `R^d` (`gaussTest_fourier`, from Mathlib's
  1547	`GaussianFourier.integral_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm_add`). The test used in the
  1548	proof (lines 65-66) is the case `w = 0`, `s = r^2/4`. `MaskedSpectralGrowth`
  1549	holds the proposition and the derivation. `ClockCopyHomog` re-issues three
  1550	existing wrappers without the supplied input.
  1551	
  1552	The wrapper `masked_spectral_growth_paper` assumes the section's standing
  1553	assumptions (lines 5-6): `H:homog`
  1554	(`HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`) and `Gamma != 0`.
  1555	It uses only the fields `Gamma_tempered`, `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and
  1556	`scaling`. The fields `dim`, `alpha0_pos`, `alpha0_lt_one`, `Gamma_radon`,
  1557	`Gamma_even`, `Gamma_posdef`, `mu_radon`, `mu_even`, `threshold` and
  1558	`alpha_range` are carried but unused. The general theorem
  1559	`masked_spectral_growth` assumes exactly these: `Gamma` and `mu` tempered
  1560	(`IsTempered`), the spectral convention `E:masked-spectral-convention`
  1561	(lines 15-19; `IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu`), the scaling
  1562	`Gamma(cA) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)` for measurable `A` and `c > 0` (written
  1563	`SpectralHomog.SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha)`, which is literally the
  1564	`scaling` field), and `Gamma != 0`. `Gamma != 0` is used only for
  1565	`M_Gamma > 0`. `masked_gaussian_transform` assumes only the spectral convention.
  1566	`translated_gauss_le` assumes the convention and the scaling. `closedBall_le`
  1567	assumes those two and the `mu`-integrability of the Gaussian. None of these
  1568	general forms restricts `alpha`.
  1569	
  1570	Implicit hypotheses made explicit:
  1571	- The manuscript's `M_Gamma < inf` is stated as `Gamma`-integrability of
  1572	  `exp(-norm(x)^2/4)`.
  1573	- A Lean Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`, so the wrappers
  1574	  conclude the integrability of both integrands of `E:masked-gaussian-transform`
  1575	  for every `y` and `r > 0`. `masked_gaussian_transform`, `spectral_gaussTest`
  1576	  and `spectral_translated_gauss` alone are identities of Lean integrals, with
  1577	  no integrability conclusion.
  1578	- The balls are `Metric.ball y r` and `Metric.closedBall y r`, and the mass
  1579	  bound is stated in `[0, inf]` as `mu(B) <= ENNReal.ofReal (C_Gamma r^alpha)`.
  1580	
  1581	The derived homogeneity is `spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`: under `H:homog`,
  1582	`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha`. It uses the fields `mu_tempered`, `spectral`
  1583	and `scaling`. Its general form is `spectralHomogeneous_of_scaling`
  1584	(`mu` tempered, the spectral convention, the scaling of `Gamma`, any real
  1585	`alpha`), and its pushforward form is `map_smul_of_scaling`. With it,
  1586	`ClockCopyHomog.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`,
  1587	`ClockCopyHomog.damped_N2_nonneg_paper` and
  1588	`ClockCopyHomog.damped_norms_finite_paper` have exactly the conclusions of
  1589	`ClockCopy.clock_copy_obstruction_paper`, `ClockCopy.damped_N2_nonneg_paper`
  1590	and `DampedNorms.damped_norms_finite_paper`, with the argument
  1591	`SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha` removed. Each is proved by applying the
  1592	existing wrapper, so the hypotheses carried but unused there are as in the
  1593	`ClockCopy` section, except that `mu_tempered`, `spectral` and the `Gamma`
  1594	scaling are now used.

  1596	Proof route:
  1597	- For the proposition, Lean follows the TeX. The exceptions:
  1598	  - The Gaussian Fourier constant (lines 56-64, derived there from the ODE
  1599	    `J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)`) comes from Mathlib.
  1600	  - The integrability of a translated Gaussian against a tempered measure
  1601	    (`integrable_gauss_of_tempered`) is proved directly from the package's
  1602	    integral form of temperedness (`IsTempered`: `int (1+norm(x))^(-k) < inf`
  1603	    for some `k`), not by the polynomial mass growth argument of lines 23-30.
  1604	- For the homogeneity, the TeX only says "Fourier uniqueness". Lean proceeds in
  1605	  three steps:
  1606	  1. It weights both `mu o (c.)^(-1)` and `c^(-alpha) mu` by `e^(-norm(xi)^2)`.
  1607	     These are finite measures because `mu` is tempered.
  1608	  2. Their characteristic functions agree. Each is a translated Gaussian
  1609	     integral against `Gamma`, by the spectral convention applied to
  1610	     `e^(-s norm(x-t)^2)`, and the two are related by the scaling of `Gamma`.
  1611	  3. `Measure.ext_of_charFun` identifies the two weighted measures, and
  1612	     `withDensity_inv_same` removes the weight.
  1613	
  1614	Refutations (`refutations/masked-spectral-growth/`):
  1615	- `ExponentShift`, `TransformFactor` and `SpectralExponent` use `d = 1`,
  1616	  `Gamma` = Lebesgue measure, `mu = delta_0`, `alpha = 0`. This is outside the
  1617	  range of `H:homog`, so they refute variants of the general theorems
  1618	  `translated_gauss_le`, `masked_gaussian_transform` and
  1619	  `spectralHomogeneous_of_scaling`, not variants of
  1620	  `masked_spectral_growth_paper`.
  1621	- `DecayConstant` and `FourierExponent` refute variants of
  1622	  `poly_mul_exp_neg_sq_le` and `gaussTest_fourier`.
  1623	
  1624	The wrapper is not instantiated in Lean at a nonzero `Gamma` satisfying all of
  1625	`H:homog`. Not formalized: the polynomial mass growth of tempered Radon
  1626	measures and the Schwartz integrability claim of lines 23-30 beyond Gaussians,

  1760	## OccupationKernelRow (whole result)
  1761	
  1762	Formalizes two lemmas of the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
  1763	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `3920258`; the file is
  1764	byte-identical at `ba01d98`, so the line numbers agree):
  1765	`L:occupation-kernel-row` (lines 291-309) with the kernel
  1766	`E:occupation-damped-kernel` (lines 282-289) and the display
  1767	`E:occupation-kernel-row` (lines 295-298), and `L:spatial-physical-pair`
  1768	(lines 12-33) with `E:spatial-physical-pair` (lines 15-17). Nothing is
  1769	supplied as a hypothesis. `Kstar` is the manuscript's formula word for word,
  1770	with `K_star(0) = 0` (line 289) and `Gamma_E` read as Mathlib's
  1771	`Real.Gamma`. `Kstar_eq_Psi` identifies it, for `u != 0`, with the averaged
  1772	clock kernel `TimeFractional.Psi a |u| (|u|/D)` (main file,
  1773	`E:averaged-clock-kernel`, line 7503), and positivity and the bound
  1774	`K_star(u) <= |u|^(-a)` are reused from `TimeFractional`.
  1775	`kstarIntegrand_integrable` proves that the defining integral converges for
  1776	`a > 0`, `D > 0`, `u != 0`. It is a separate theorem, not a conjunct of the
  1777	headline. The headline `occupation_kernel_row` (for `0 < a < 1`, `D > 0`)
  1778	proves exactly nine conjuncts: evenness; positivity off zero; local
  1779	integrability; strict decrease on `(0,inf)` (the TeX says "decreasing", which
  1780	this implies); `K_star(u) <= |u|^(-a)` off zero; interval integrability of
  1781	each row `t -> K_star(s-t)`, `s` in `[0,1]`, on `[0,1]`; that
  1782	`R_star = 2 int_0^(1/2) K_star` is the greatest element of the set of row
  1783	values over `s` in `[0,1]` (so the maximum exists, equals `R_star` and is
  1784	attained at `s = 1/2`); interval integrability of `K_star` on `[0,1/2]`; and
  1785	`0 < R_star` (a real number, hence finite). `occupation_kernel_row_paper`
  1786	states this under the section's standing assumptions (lines 4-10: `H:homog`
  1787	as `HomogCovariance d alpha a Gamma mu` with `a = alpha0`, `Gamma != 0`,
  1788	`D = (4 - alpha) - 2a`). `D > 0` and `a < 1` are derived from `H:homog`
  1789	(`a + alpha < 2`, `a < 1`); `Gamma != 0` and the other clauses of `H:homog`
  1790	are carried and not used. The TeX proof shows the row bound
  1791	`Phi(s) + Phi(1-s) <= 2 Phi(1/2)` by concavity of `Phi`. Lean proves it
  1792	instead by a shift comparison that uses the same monotonicity of `K_star`
  1793	(`Phi_sum_le_of_le_half`, auxiliary). For `L:spatial-physical-pair`,
  1794	`pairMeasure Gamma = volume.prod Gamma` on `R^d x R^d` (`EuclideanSpace`),
  1795	and `pairing` is the lower Lebesgue integral of `f(x) h(x-y)` for
  1796	`[0,inf]`-valued `f, h`. This allows arbitrary `[0,inf]`-valued functions,
  1797	a class that contains the TeX's finite Borel representatives.
  1798	`spatial_physical_pair` assumes only that `Gamma` is locally finite, for
  1799	any `d`, and proves four conjuncts: sigma-finiteness of `nu`; representative
  1800	independence under Lebesgue-a.e. changes of `f` and `h`; `nu`-a.e.
  1801	measurability of `f(x) h(x-y)` for Lebesgue-a.e.-measurable `f, h` (the TeX's
  1802	"measurable in the `nu` completion"); and the transfer of Lebesgue-a.e.
  1803	convergence of real sequences `F n -> G` (indexed by `N`) to `nu`-a.e.
  1804	convergence at `x` and at `x - y`. `ae_pair_of_ae` is the null-set transfer
  1805	of the proof (lines 26-29), for an arbitrary a.e. property.
  1806	`spatial_physical_pair_paper` states it under `HomogCovariance` and
  1807	`Gamma != 0`; only local finiteness of `Gamma` is used. The sentence
  1808	"Signed pairings will be used only after absolute convergence" (lines 31-32)
  1809	is a usage convention, not a claim, and is not formalized. The real-valued
  1810	kernel-integral conclusions include integrability; the physical pairing
  1811	remains an extended nonnegative integral and need not be finite.

    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤

    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/

    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re

    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ

   152	/-- Pointwise shell majorant (auxiliary to the Lean proof route): if `F ≤ c 0` when

   155	theorem le_shellSum {E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] (y x : E) (F : ENNReal)
   156	    (c : ℕ → ENNReal) (h0 : ‖x - y‖ ≤ 1 → F ≤ c 0)
   157	    (hs : ∀ n : ℕ, (2 : ℝ) ^ n ≤ ‖x - y‖ → ‖x - y‖ ≤ 2 ^ (n + 1) → F ≤ c (n + 1)) :
   158	    F ≤ ∑' j, (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)).indicator (fun _ => c j) x := by
   159	  by_cases h1 : ‖x - y‖ ≤ 1
   160	  · refine le_trans ?_ (ENNReal.le_tsum 0)
   161	    rw [Set.indicator_of_mem (by simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm] using h1)]
   162	    exact h0 h1
   163	  · replace h1 := not_le.mp h1
   164	    obtain ⟨n, hn1, hn2⟩ := exists_nat_pow_near h1.le (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 2)
   165	    refine le_trans ?_ (ENNReal.le_tsum (n + 1))
   166	    rw [Set.indicator_of_mem (by simpa [mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm] using hn2.le)]
   167	    exact hs n hn1 hn2.le

   172	    [OpensMeasurableSpace E] (ν : Measure E) (y : E) (c : ℕ → ENNReal) :
   173	    ∫⁻ x, ∑' j, (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)).indicator (fun _ => c j) x ∂ν =
   174	      ∑' j, c j * ν (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)) := by
   175	  rw [lintegral_tsum fun j => (measurable_const.indicator measurableSet_closedBall).aemeasurable]
   176	  congr 1; funext j
   177	  exact lintegral_indicator_const measurableSet_closedBall _

   180	radius `r + ε` and let `ε ↓ 0`). Any measure on a pseudometric space. -/
   181	theorem closedBall_le {E : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] (ν : Measure E)
   182	    {C α : ℝ} (hgrowth : ∀ y : E, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ν (ball y r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ α))
   183	    (y : E) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
   184	    ν (closedBall y R) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * R ^ α) := by
   185	  have hT : Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (C * (R + ε) ^ α)) (𝓝[>] 0)
   186	      (𝓝 (ENNReal.ofReal (C * R ^ α))) := by
   187	    apply ENNReal.tendsto_ofReal
   188	    apply Tendsto.mono_left _ nhdsWithin_le_nhds
   189	    have : Continuous fun ε : ℝ => R + ε := by fun_prop
   190	    have hc : ContinuousAt (fun ε : ℝ => C * (R + ε) ^ α) 0 := by
   191	      apply ContinuousAt.mul continuousAt_const
   192	      apply ContinuousAt.rpow_const this.continuousAt
   193	      left; simp [hR.ne']
   194	    simpa using hc.tendsto
   195	  apply ge_of_tendsto hT
   196	  filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with ε hε
   197	  calc ν (closedBall y R) ≤ ν (ball y (R + ε)) :=
   198	        measure_mono (closedBall_subset_ball (by linarith [show (0:ℝ) < ε from hε]))
   199	    _ ≤ _ := hgrowth y _ (by linarith [show (0:ℝ) < ε from hε])

   205	    (y : E) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (hc : ∀ j, 0 ≤ c j) :
   206	    ∑' j, ENNReal.ofReal (c j) * ν (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j)) ≤
   207	      ∑' j, ENNReal.ofReal (c j * C * ((2 : ℝ) ^ α) ^ j) := by
   208	  apply ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum; intro j
   209	  calc ENNReal.ofReal (c j) * ν (closedBall y ((2 : ℝ) ^ j))
   210	      ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c j) * ENNReal.ofReal (C * ((2 : ℝ) ^ j) ^ α) :=
   211	        by gcongr; exact closedBall_le ν hgrowth y (by positivity)

     2	\label{S:wave-variance}
     3	
     4	We now apply the covariance and temporal estimates of
     5	Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance} to the full wave phase. We retain
     6	Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, write $a = \alpha_0$, and choose and fix
     7	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-gamma-range}
     8	  0 < \gamma < \min\left(\frac12,\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\right).
     9	\end{equation}
    10	The interval is nonempty because $\alpha+a < 2$. We use $\langle\xi\rangle =
    11	\sqrt{1+|\xi|^2}$ and set
    12	\begin{equation}\label{E:variance-scale-profile}
    13	  B_\alpha(h) =
    14	  \begin{cases}
    15	    1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    16	    1+\log(1/h), & \alpha = 1,\\
    17	    h^{1-\alpha}, & \alpha > 1,
    18	  \end{cases}
    19	  \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    20	\end{equation}
    21	
    22	\subsection{A scalar row estimate for a measure}
    23	
    24	Let $\nu$ be a positive Radon measure satisfying
    25	\begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-translated-growth}
    26	  \nu(B(y,r)) \le C r^\alpha,
    27	  \qquad y \in \R^d,\quad r > 0,
    28	\end{equation}
    29	where $C \ge 0$. If the estimate is initially known for open balls, apply it at
    30	radius $r+\epsilon$ and let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$ to obtain the closed-ball
    31	estimate. Neither evenness nor a density is assumed here.
    32	Using~\eqref{E:masked-frequency-pair}, define
    33	\begin{align}
    34	  \Phi_h(\xi,\eta)
    35	  &:= \frac{\mathcal{Q}_h(|\xi|,|\eta|)}
    36	  {\langle\xi\rangle\langle\eta\rangle},
    37	  \label{E:frequency-row-kernel}\\
    38	  J_h(\xi)
    39	  &:= \langle\xi\rangle^{2\gamma}
    40	  \int_{\R^d}\Phi_h(\xi,\xi-\lambda)\nu(\ud\lambda).
    41	  \label{E:frequency-row-integral}
    42	\end{align}
    43	These are initially nonnegative extended integrals. In particular, the notation
    44	denotes a pushforward of $\nu$, not integration against an assumed spectral
    45	density.
    46	
    47	\begin{proposition}[Uniform scalar row]\label{P:frequency-row}
    48	  There is a finite $K = K(\alpha,a,\gamma)$, independent of $d,\nu,C,h$ and
    49	  $\xi$, such that
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-row-bound}
    51	    \sup_{\xi\in\R^d}J_h(\xi) \le K C B_\alpha(h),
    52	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{proposition}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  If $C = 0$, a countable covering by finite balls gives $\nu = 0$, and the
    58	  result is immediate. Suppose $C > 0$. For each $\xi$, let $\nu_\xi$ be the
    59	  pushforward under $\lambda \mapsto \eta = \xi-\lambda$. Then $\nu_\xi(B(0,R))
    60	  \le CR^\alpha$. For $q \ge 1$, put
    61	  \[
    62	    A_\xi(q) = \int_{|\eta|\le5q}\langle\eta\rangle^{-1}
    63	    \nu_\xi(\ud\eta).
    64	  \]
    65	  Choose $N = \lceil\log_2(5q)\rceil$, so $5q \le 2^N < 10q$. Splitting into the
    66	  unit ball and the annuli $2^j < |\eta| \le 2^{j+1}$ gives
    67	  \[
    68	    A_\xi(q) \le C\left(1+2^\alpha
    69	    \sum_{j=0}^{N-1}2^{j(\alpha-1)}\right).
    70	  \]
    71	  The geometric sum is bounded when $\alpha < 1$, is $N$ when $\alpha = 1$, and
    72	  is at most $2^{N(\alpha-1)}/(2^{\alpha-1}-1)$ when $\alpha > 1$. Hence,
    73	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}
    74	    A_\xi(q) \le K_\alpha C
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1, & \alpha < 1,\\
    77	      1+\log q, & \alpha = 1,\\
    78	      q^{\alpha-1}, & \alpha > 1,
    79	    \end{cases}
    80	  \end{equation}
    81	  with a constant depending only on $\alpha$.
    82	
    83	  Set $q = \max(1,|\xi|)$ and $\epsilon = 1-2\gamma > 0$. On $|\lambda| \le 4q$
    84	  we have $|\eta| \le 5q$. Both bracket powers in $\mathcal{Q}_h$ are at most
    85	  one, since $a-1 < 0$. The contribution of this region to $J_h(\xi)$ is at most
    86	  \[
    87	    2\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q)
    88	    \le 2q^{-\epsilon}A_\xi(q).
    89	  \]
    90	  If $\alpha < 1$, this is uniformly bounded
    91	  by~\eqref{E:frequency-inverse-bessel}. If $\alpha = 1$, the bound follows from
    92	  \[
    93	    e^{-\epsilon u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\epsilon},
    94	    \qquad u = \log q \ge 0,
    95	  \]
    96	  since $u e^{-\epsilon u}$ has maximum $1/(e\epsilon)$. If $\alpha > 1$, the
    97	  remaining power is $q^{\alpha+2\gamma-2}$, whose exponent is negative
    98	  by~\eqref{E:variance-gamma-range}. Thus, the near contribution is at most a
    99	  constant times $C$ in all three cases.
   100	
   101	  On the far region write $r = |\lambda| > 4q$. Then
   102	  \[
   103	    |\eta| \ge \frac{3r}4,\qquad
   104	    \big||\eta|-|\xi|\big| \ge \frac r2,\qquad
   105	    |\eta|+|\xi| \ge \frac r2.
   106	  \]
   107	  Each oscillatory bracket is at least $\langle hr\rangle/2$, whereas
   108	  $\langle\eta\rangle^{-1} \le 4/(3r)$ and $\langle\xi\rangle^{-\epsilon} \le
   109	  1$. Consequently, the far contribution is at most
   110	  \[
   111	    \frac43\,2^{2-a}\int_{|\lambda|>4q}
   112	    |\lambda|^{-1}\langle h|\lambda|\rangle^{a-1}\nu(\ud\lambda).
   113	  \]
   114	  Enlarge the domain to $|\lambda| > 1$ and split it into dyadic annuli.
   115	  Applying~\eqref{E:frequency-translated-growth} to their masses bounds this
   116	  expression by a constant depending only on $\alpha,a$ times $C S(h)$, where
   117	  \[
   118	    S(h) = \sum_{j=0}^\infty
   119	    2^{j(\alpha-1)}\langle h2^j\rangle^{a-1}.
   120	  \]
   121	  Choose $L = \lfloor\log_2(1/h)\rfloor \ge 0$. For $j \le L$ the bracket power
   122	  is at most one. For $j \ge L+1$ it is at most $(h2^j)^{a-1}$. Since
   123	  $\alpha+a-2 < 0$, the tail is
   124	  \[
   125	    \frac{h^{a-1}2^{(L+1)(\alpha+a-2)}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}
   126	    \le \frac{h^{1-\alpha}}{1-2^{\alpha+a-2}}.
   127	  \]
   128	  The inequality uses $2^{L+1} > 1/h$ and the negative exponent. The finite sum
   129	  is bounded by $1/(1-2^{\alpha-1})$ for $\alpha < 1$, by $1+\log_2(1/h)$ for
   130	  $\alpha = 1$, and by
   131	  \[
   132	    \frac{2^{\alpha-1}h^{1-\alpha}}{2^{\alpha-1}-1}
   133	  \]
   134	  for $\alpha > 1$. Since $h^{1-\alpha} \le 1$ in the first case, we obtain
   135	  $S(h) \le K_{\alpha,a}B_\alpha(h)$. Combining the near and far bounds, and
   136	  using $B_\alpha(h) \ge 1$, proves the assertion and finiteness of the original
   137	  integral. All constants arose from numerical shell estimates and are
   138	  independent of $d$. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}.
   139	\end{proof}

   141	\begin{corollary}[A time exponent above one half]\label{C:frequency-time}
   142	  For every
   143	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variance-beta-range}
   144	    \frac12 < \beta < \min\left(1-\frac a2,
   145	    \frac{3-a-\alpha}{2}\right),
   146	  \end{equation}
   147	  there is a finite $K_\beta = K_\beta(\alpha,a,\gamma,\beta)$ such that
   148	  \begin{equation}\label{E:frequency-time-bound}
   149	    h^{2-a}\sup_\xi J_h(\xi) \le K_\beta C h^{2\beta},
   150	    \qquad 0 < h \le 1.
   151	  \end{equation}
   152	\end{corollary}
   153	
   154	\begin{proof}
   155	  Both upper endpoints in~\eqref{E:variance-beta-range} exceed one half, by $a <
   156	  1$ and $\alpha+a < 2$. If $\alpha < 1$, use $2-a > 2\beta$ in
   157	  Proposition~\ref{P:frequency-row}. If $\alpha > 1$, use $3-a-\alpha > 2\beta$.
   158	  For $\alpha = 1$, set $\delta = 2-a-2\beta > 0$ and $u = \log(1/h)$. Then
   159	  \[
   160	    h^\delta(1+\log(1/h))
   161	    = e^{-\delta u}(1+u) \le 1+\frac1{e\delta}.
   162	  \]
   163	  This absorbs the critical logarithm. No endpoint value of $\beta$ is used.
   164	  This proves Corollary~\ref{C:frequency-time}.
   165	\end{proof}

   251	  have hm : AEStronglyMeasurable (integrand a f) (μ.prod μ) := by

   262	    simp only [integrand, norm_mul, RCLike.norm_conj, RCLike.norm_ofReal,

   264	    rw [ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by positivity), ENNReal.ofReal_mul (norm_nonneg _)]

   283	  have hnn : 0 ≤ ∫ t, ‖f t‖ ^ 2 ∂μ := integral_nonneg fun t => by positivity

   288	        rw [ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hR, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hnn]

   427	/-- Auxiliary: a bound `‖Φ‖ ≤ M` forces `M ≥ 0`. -/
   428	theorem M_nonneg_of_bound (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M) : 0 ≤ M := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hΦb 0)

   433	    (hΦb : ∀ u, ‖Φ u‖ ≤ M) (v : ℝ) : Integrable (fun u => Φ (u + v) * conj (Φ u)) := by
   434	  have hM := M_nonneg_of_bound hΦb
   435	  refine Integrable.mono' (g := (Icc s (s + h)).indicator (fun _ => M * M)) ?_ ?_ ?_
   436	  · exact (continuous_const.integrableOn_Icc).integrable_indicator measurableSet_Icc
   437	  · exact ((hΦm.comp (measurable_add_const v)).mul
   438	      (Complex.continuous_conj.measurable.comp hΦm)).aestronglyMeasurable
   439	  · refine ae_of_all _ fun u => ?_
   440	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   441	    · rw [indicator_of_mem hu, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj]
   442	      exact mul_le_mul (hΦb _) (hΦb _) (norm_nonneg _) hM
   443	    · rw [indicator_of_notMem hu, hΦ0 u hu, map_zero, mul_zero, norm_zero]

   456	      by_contra hc
   457	      obtain ⟨hc1, hc2⟩ := not_or.mp hc

   462	        by_contra h'

   492	    (continuous_const.integrableOn_Icc).integrable_indicator measurableSet_Icc
   493	  have hi2 : Integrable ((Ioc (s + h - w) (s + h - v)).indicator (fun _ => M * M)) :=

   502	      indicator_nonneg (fun _ _ => mul_nonneg hM hM) u
   503	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   504	    · by_cases hw : u + w ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   505	      · have hvI : u + v ∈ Icc s (s + h) := ⟨by linarith [hu.1], by linarith [hw.2]⟩

   514	      · rw [hΦ0 _ hw, zero_mul, sub_zero]
   515	        by_cases hv' : u + v ∈ Icc s (s + h)
   516	        · have hmem : u ∈ Ioc (s + h - w) (s + h - v) := by
   517	            refine ⟨?_, by linarith [hv'.2]⟩
   518	            by_contra hc
   519	            exact hw ⟨by linarith [hu.1], by linarith⟩
   520	          rw [indicator_of_mem hmem, norm_mul, Complex.norm_conj]
   521	          have := mul_le_mul (hΦb (u + v)) (hΦb u) (norm_nonneg _) hM
   522	          linarith
   523	        · rw [hΦ0 _ hv', zero_mul, norm_zero]
   524	          linarith
   525	    · rw [hΦ0 u hu, map_zero, mul_zero, mul_zero, sub_zero, norm_zero]
   526	      linarith
   527	  refine (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le (hi1.add hi2) (ae_of_all _ hpt)).trans ?_
   528	  rw [integral_add' hi1 hi2, integral_indicator_const _ measurableSet_Icc,
   529	    integral_indicator_const _ measurableSet_Ioc, Real.volume_real_Icc, Real.volume_real_Ioc,
   530	    smul_eq_mul, smul_eq_mul]
   531	  rw [show s + h - s = h by ring, show s + h - v - (s + h - w) = w - v by ring,
   532	    max_eq_left hh, max_eq_left (by linarith)]
   533	  apply le_of_eq
   534	  ring

1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]
   121	  For scalar Schwartz functions this follows by Fourier inversion and absolute
   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
   129	  \[
   130	    \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2
   131	    \le c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   132	  \]
   133	  Integrating against $\mu$ and applying Tonelli's theorem proves
   134	  \eqref{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}. Its right side is finite by Schwartz decay
   135	  and temperedness of $\nu_R$. This proves
   136	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}.
   137	\end{proof}

   139	\subsection{Temporal completion and the original noise}
   140	
   141	\begin{lemma}[Temporal covariance completion]\label{L:masked-time-completion}
   142	  Let $T > 0$. The form
   143	  \[
   144	    \langle f,g\rangle_a

   167	    = \int_{-\infty}^{\min(t,s)}2\lambda
   168	    e^{-\lambda(t-u)}e^{-\lambda(s-u)}\ud u.

   171	  exchanges for compact smooth tests are absolutely integrable because the

   208	\begin{proof}

   212	    h(z) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}\widehat{f}(\xi)
   213	    \overline{\widehat{g}(\xi)}\ud\xi.
   214	  \]

216	  \[
   217	    \int e^{i\xi\cdot z}h(z)\ud z
   218	    = (2\pi)^d\widehat{f}(-\xi)\overline{\widehat{g}(-\xi)}.
   219	  \]

   257	\begin{proposition}[A physical mask need not preserve noise-null tests]
   258	  \label{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}
   259	  In the admissible case $d = 2$, $\alpha = 1$, $0 < a < 1$ and $\Gamma =
   260	  \delta_0(\ud x_1)\ud x_2$, there is a real compact smooth mask $\zeta$ such
   261	  that no finite $C$ satisfies $\E W(\zeta F)^2 \le C\E W(F)^2$ for every
   262	  compact smooth test $F$.

   265	\begin{proof}
   266	  Fourier inversion on Schwartz tests gives $\mu =
   267	  (2\pi)^{-1}\ud\xi_1\delta_0(\ud\xi_2)$ in the stated spectral convention. The
   268	  measure $\Gamma$ is nonnegative, even, positive definite and tempered, with
   269	  $\Gamma(cA) = c\Gamma(A)$. It therefore satisfies Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}
   270	  with $\alpha = 1$. This is not spatial white noise in dimension two. For real
   271	  compact smooth $g$, its spatial covariance is, by ordinary Fubini,
   272	  \[
   273	    V(g) = \int_\R\left(\int_\R g(x_1,x_2)\ud x_2\right)^2\ud x_1.
   274	  \]

   276	  outside $[-2,2]$. For example, on $1 < r = |x| < 2$ use
   277	  \[
   278	    \chi(x) = \frac{e^{-1/(2-r)}}{e^{-1/(2-r)}+e^{-1/(r-1)}}.
   279	  \]

   281	  smoothly. Let $I_\chi = \int(\chi')^2 > 0$ and $J_\chi = \int\chi^4 > 0$.
   282	  Positivity of $I_\chi$ follows because $\chi$ is not constant, and $J_\chi \ge
   283	  2$. Put $g(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi''(x_2)$ and $\zeta(x) = \chi(x_1)\chi(x_2)$.
   284	  Their unmasked marginal vanishes since $\int\chi'' = 0$, whereas integration
   285	  by parts gives the masked marginal $-I_\chi\chi(x_1)^2$. Thus, $V(g) = 0$ and
   286	  $V(\zeta g) = J_\chi I_\chi^2 > 0$. For a nonzero nonnegative $\tau \in
   287	  C_c^\infty(0,T)$, set $F(t,x) = \tau(t)g(x)$. The temporal factor
   288	  $\|\tau\|_a^2$ is finite and strictly positive because its nonnegative
   289	  integrand is positive on a set of positive two-dimensional measure.
   290	  Consequently, the full unmasked variance is zero and the masked variance is
   291	  positive. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:masked-quotient-obstruction}.

   294	\subsection{Temporal modulation and continuous wave factors}
   295	
   296	Write $\langle x\rangle = \sqrt{1+x^2}$. Let $I = [s,s+h] \subset [0,T]$, with
   297	$0 < h \le 1$. Norms below are those of the complexified temporal completion in
   298	Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion}.
   299	
   300	\begin{lemma}[Modulated amplitudes]\label{L:masked-temporal-modulation}
   301	  Let $A \in C^1(I;\mathbb{C})$, $M = \sup_I|A|$ and $D = \sup_I|A'|$. For every
   302	  real $\omega$,
   303	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-temporal-modulation}
   304	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   305	    \le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\langle h\omega\rangle^{a-1},
   306	    \qquad C_0(a) = \frac{16}{1-a}.
   307	  \end{equation}
   308	  The bound is uniform in $T,s,h,A$ and $\omega$.
   309	\end{lemma}
   310	
   311	\begin{proof}
   312	  Put $c(v) = \int_s^{s+h-v}A(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u$ for $0 \le v \le h$.
   313	  Differentiation at the moving endpoint gives
   314	  \[
   315	    c'(v) = -A(s+h)\overline{A(s+h-v)}
   316	    +\int_s^{s+h-v}A'(u+v)\overline{A(u)}\ud u.
   317	  \]
   318	  Thus, $c(h) = 0$, $|c(v)| \le hM^2$ and $|c'(v)| \le M^2+hMD$. Splitting the
   319	  covariance square into its two conjugate triangles gives
   320	  \[
   321	    \|1_IA(t)e^{i\omega t}\|_a^2
   322	    = 2\operatorname{Re}\int_0^h v^{-a}e^{i\omega v}c(v)\ud v
   323	    = 2h^{2-a}\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 y^{-a}e^{i\omega hy}f(y)\ud y,
   324	  \]
   325	  where $f(y) = c(hy)/h$. Set $K = M+hD$. Then $f(1) = 0$ and $|f|,|f'| \le
   326	  K^2$. If $K = 0$ the assertion is immediate. If $|\omega h| \le 1$, the last
   327	  integral is at most $K^2/(1-a)$ in absolute value, and $\langle\omega
   328	  h\rangle^{a-1} \ge 2^{(a-1)/2}$. The claimed constant is sufficient in this
   329	  case.
   330	
   331	  Now suppose $k = |\omega h| > 1$. On $[0,1/k]$ the integral is at most
   332	  $K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. On $[1/k,1]$, integrate the exponential by parts. The
   333	  endpoint at one vanishes, while the other endpoint contributes at most
   334	  $K^2k^{a-1}$. The derivative integral, divided by $k$, is bounded by
   335	  \[
   336	    \frac{K^2}k\left(a\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a-1}\ud y
   337	    +\int_{1/k}^1 y^{-a}\ud y\right)
   338	    \le K^2 k^{a-1}\left(1+\frac1{1-a}\right).
   339	  \]
   340	  Here $k^{-1} \le k^{a-1}$ since $a > 0$. The total is at most
   341	  $4K^2k^{a-1}/(1-a)$. Finally, $k^{a-1} \le \sqrt{2}\langle\omega
   342	  h\rangle^{a-1}$ and $8\sqrt{2} \le 16$. Including the factor $2h^{2-a}$ proves
   343	  the bound for either sign of $\omega$. This proves
   344	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation}.
   345	\end{proof}

   347	\begin{lemma}[Correlated trigonometric products]\label{L:masked-trig-products}
   348	  Let $r,\rho \ge 0$. Let $P_r$ be either $\cos(rt)$ or $\sin(rt)$, and let
   349	  $Q_\rho$ be either $\cos(\rho t)$ or $\sin(\rho t)$. With the amplitude and
   350	  constant above,
   351	  \begin{align}
   352	    \|1_IAP_rQ_\rho\|_a^2
   353	    &\le C_0(a)h^{2-a}(M+hD)^2\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   354	    \label{E:masked-trig-products}\\
   355	    \mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho)
   356	    &:= \langle h(r-\rho)\rangle^{a-1}
   357	    +\langle h(r+\rho)\rangle^{a-1}.
   358	    \label{E:masked-frequency-pair}
   359	  \end{align}
   360	\end{lemma}
   361	
   362	\begin{proof}
   363	  Expanding the two trigonometric factors gives four complex exponential modes
   364	  with frequencies $\sigma r+\tau\rho$, $\sigma,\tau \in \{-1,1\}$, and
   365	  coefficients of absolute value $1/4$. In a Hilbert space,
   366	  \[
   367	    \left\|\sum_j c_jv_j\right\|^2
   368	    \le \left(\sum_j|c_j|\right)\sum_j|c_j|\|v_j\|^2.
   369	  \]
   370	  The first coefficient sum is one. Apply
   371	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-temporal-modulation} to each mode. Two frequencies have
   372	  absolute value $|r-\rho|$ and two have absolute value $r+\rho$. This gives one
   373	  half of the asserted right side, and hence the bound. Repeated or zero
   374	  frequencies are permitted; no orthogonality or independence of the modes is
   375	  used. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products}.
   376	\end{proof}
   377	
   378	\begin{lemma}[Continuous sine factors]\label{L:masked-continuous-wave}
   379	  Define $c_r(t) = \cos(rt)$ and
   380	  \[
   381	    b_r(t) = \langle r\rangle\frac{\sin(rt)}r\quad(r > 0),
   382	    \qquad b_0(t) = t.
   383	  \]
   384	  For $F_r \in \{c_r,b_r\}$ and $G_\rho \in \{c_\rho,b_\rho\}$,
   385	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-continuous-wave}
   386	    \|1_IF_rG_\rho\|_a^2
   387	    \le C_1(a)(1+T)^4h^{2-a}\mathcal{Q}_h(r,\rho),
   388	    \qquad C_1(a) = 4\cdot3^{1-a}C_0(a).
   389	  \end{equation}
   390	\end{lemma}
   391	
   392	\begin{proof}
   393	  For $r \ge 1$, $b_r$ is a sine times a coefficient at most $\sqrt{2}$. For $0
   394	  \le r \le 1$, the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
   395	  \[
   396	    b_r(t) = t\langle r\rangle\int_0^1\cos(vrt)\ud v.
   397	  \]
   398	  This includes $r = 0$. Hence, a product $F_rG_\rho$ is a scalar coefficient of
   399	  absolute value at most two times a normalized integral of
   400	  $t^jP_{r'}(t)Q_{\rho'}(t)$, where $j \in \{0,1,2\}$ and $|r'-r|,|\rho'-\rho|
   401	  \le 1$. The integral is over zero, one or two copies of $[0,1]$; with no
   402	  averages, use a one-point probability space. Its parameter dependence is
   403	  continuous in $L^2(0,T)$ by dominated convergence.
   404	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-time-completion} makes it continuous in $H_a$ as well.
   405	  Thus, the averages are Bochner integrals, and their $H_a$ images agree with
   406	  the pointwise averages by continuity of the inclusion. Hilbert Jensen bounds
   407	  the squared norm of an average by the average of the squared norms.
   408	
   409	  Apply Lemma~\ref{L:masked-trig-products} to each integrand with $A(t) = t^j$.
   410	  For $j = 0,1,2$, respectively, $M+hD$ is at most $1$, $T+1$ and $T^2+2T$. In
   411	  every case $(M+hD)^2 \le (1+T)^4$. For real $x,e$, the triangle inequality and
   412	  its reverse imply
   413	  \[
   414	    \frac{\langle x\rangle}{1+|e|}
   415	    \le \langle x+e\rangle \le (1+|e|)\langle x\rangle.
   416	  \]
   417	  The changes in $h(r\pm\rho)$ have magnitude at most two, since $h \le 1$.
   418	  Because $a-1 < 0$, each altered bracket to the power $a-1$ is at most
   419	  $3^{1-a}$ times the original one. Apply these comparisons, Hilbert Jensen and
   420	  the squared scalar coefficient bound four to obtain
   421	  \eqref{E:masked-continuous-wave}. This proves
   422	  Lemma~\ref{L:masked-continuous-wave}.
   423	\end{proof}

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.

    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.

    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.

  1675	`{cos(rho t), sin(rho t)}`, the bound `E:masked-trig-products`,
  1676	`||1_I A P_r Q_rho||_a^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)`, with
  1677	`Q_h` as in `E:masked-frequency-pair` and `<x> = sqrt(1+x^2)`. All four
  1678	`cos`/`sin` combinations are covered, together with every step of the
  1679	proof: the four-mode expansion (coefficients of absolute value `1/4`,
  1680	frequencies `+-r +- rho`), the Hilbert-space inequality
  1681	`||sum c_j v_j||^2 <= (sum |c_j|) sum |c_j| ||v_j||^2`, and the frequency

  1684	the complexified temporal completion `H_a^C` of `L:masked-time-completion`,
  1685	and functions enter it through the linear inclusion of `L^2(0,T)`. In Lean,
  1686	`E` stands for that completion (a complex inner product space in the

  4098	  summary: "For real alpha, c > 0 and natural d: (c^(-1))^(-(d - alpha)) * (pi/(1/4))^(d/2) = c^(-alpha) * (pi/(1/(4c^2)))^(d/2)."

  4104	  kind: theorem
  4105	  summary: "If mu is tempered, IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu and SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha) (Gamma(cA) = c^(d-alpha) Gamma(A)), then for c > 0: mu.map (c . ) = ENNReal.ofReal (c^(-alpha)) . mu."

  4111	  kind: theorem
  4112	  summary: "If mu is tempered, IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu and SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha), then SpectralHomogeneous mu alpha: mu(cA) = c^alpha mu(A) for measurable A and c > 0."
  4113	  keywords: [spectral-homogeneity, fourier-uniqueness]
  4114	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedSpectralGrowth.lean

  4157	  status: internal
  4158	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-spectral-growth-masked-gaussian-transform
  4159	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedSpectralGrowth.masked_gaussian_transform
  4160	  kind: theorem
  4161	  summary: "If IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, y in R^d and r > 0: (integral over mu of exp(-(norm(xi - y)^2/r^2)) : C) = (r/(2 sqrt(pi)))^d * integral over Gamma of exp(-(r^2 norm(x)^2/4)) * cexp(-(I <y,x>))."

  4169	  keywords: [spectral-measure, gaussian-bound]
  4170	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedSpectralGrowth.lean

  4174	  kind: theorem
  4175	  summary: "If IsSpectralMeasure Gamma mu, SpectralHomogeneous Gamma (d - alpha), y, r > 0 and xi -> exp(-(norm(xi - y)^2/r^2)) is mu-integrable: mu (closedBall y r) <= ENNReal.ofReal (CGamma Gamma * r^alpha)."

  4182	  summary: "Gamma, mu tempered, spectral, Gamma(cA)=c^(d-alpha)Gamma(A), Gamma != 0: e^(-|x|^2/4) Gamma-integrable, MGamma > 0; for y, r > 0: both integrands integrable, transform holds, 0 <= int e^(-|xi-y|^2/r^2)dmu <= r^alpha MGamma/(2sqrt(pi))^d; mu of open/closed ball <= CGamma r^alpha."
  4183	  keywords: [spectral-measure, ball-mass]
  4184	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedSpectralGrowth.lean

  4190	  keywords: [spectral-measure, ball-mass]
  4191	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedSpectralGrowth.lean

  4218	  kind: theorem
  4219	  summary: "For 0 < a < 1, T > 0 and real f in L^2(0,T) (MemLp f 2 on [0,T]): (t,s) -> f t * f s * |t-s|^(-a) is integrable on [0,T]^2 and int_[0,T] int_[0,T] f(t) f(s) |t-s|^(-a) <= 2 T^(1-a)/(1-a) * int_[0,T] f^2 (E:masked-time-schur, double-integral form)."
  4220	  keywords: [time-schur, temporal-completion]
  4221	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4222	  status: reusable
  4223	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/time-schur-time-schur-complex
  4224	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.TimeSchur.time_schur_complex
  4225	  kind: theorem
  4226	  summary: "For 0 < a < 1, T > 0 and complex f in L^2(0,T): (t,s) -> f t * conj(f s) * |t-s|^(-a) is integrable on [0,T]^2 and |timeForm a T f f| <= 2 T^(1-a)/(1-a) * int_[0,T] |f|^2 (E:masked-time-schur after complexification, double-integral form)."
  4227	  keywords: [time-schur, complexified-form]
  4228	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4229	  status: reusable
  4230	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/time-schur-time-schur-rclike

  4232	  kind: theorem
  4233	  summary: "For any RCLike field K, a < 1, 0 <= T and f : R -> K in L^2(0,T): integrand a f is integrable on [0,T]^2 and |int_[0,T] int_[0,T] f(t) conj(f s) |t-s|^(-a)| <= 2 T^(1-a)/(1-a) * int_[0,T] |f|^2 (general Schur bound)."
  4234	  keywords: [time-schur, schur-bound]
  4235	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4236	  status: reusable
  4237	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/time-schur-time-form
  4238	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.TimeSchur.timeForm
  4239	  kind: definition
  4240	  summary: "timeForm a T f g = int_[0,T] int_[0,T] f(t) conj(g s) |t-s|^(-a) ds dt, an iterated Bochner integral (Lean's 0 if not integrable): the complexified temporal form of L:masked-time-completion."
  4241	  keywords: [temporal-form, complexified-form]
  4242	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4243	  status: reusable
  4244	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/time-schur-kern

  4248	  keywords: [temporal-kernel, fractional-kernel]
  4249	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4250	  status: reusable
  4251	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/time-schur-integral-row
  4252	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.TimeSchur.integral_row
  4253	  kind: theorem
  4254	  summary: "For a < 1 and t in [0,T]: s -> |t-s|^(-a) is integrable on [0,T] and int_[0,T] |t-s|^(-a) ds = (t^(1-a) + (T-t)^(1-a))/(1-a) (the exact row integral)."
  4255	  keywords: [row-integral, time-schur]
  4256	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4257	  status: reusable

  4260	  kind: theorem
  4261	  summary: "For a < 1 and t in [0,T]: lintegral over [0,T] of ofReal(|t-s|^(-a)) ds <= ofReal(2 T^(1-a)/(1-a)) (the row bound)."
  4262	  keywords: [row-integral, time-schur]
  4263	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/TimeSchur.lean
  4264	  status: reusable
  4265	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/time-schur-schur-lintegral

  4335	# --- MaskedModulation (StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean) ---
  4336	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-masked-temporal-modulation-paper
  4337	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.masked_temporal_modulation_paper
  4338	  kind: theorem
  4339	  summary: "With 0<a<1, T>0, 0<h<=1, 0<=s, s+h<=T, A C^1 on I=[s,s+h], M=sup_I|A|, D=sup_I|A'|, real omega: F=1_I A e^(i omega t) gives an integrable integrand on [0,T]^2 and |timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1)."
  4340	  keywords: [temporal-modulation, oscillatory-bound]
  4341	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4342	  status: reusable
  4343	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-modulation-bound
  4344	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.modulation_bound
  4345	  kind: theorem
  4346	  summary: "If 0<a<1, h>0, 0<=s, s+h<=T, A continuous on I=[s,s+h], |A|<=M on I and |A x - A y| <= D|x-y| on I: for every real omega, F=1_I A e^(i omega t) has integrable integrand on [0,T]^2 and |timeForm a T F F| <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 <h omega>^(a-1)."
  4347	  keywords: [temporal-modulation, oscillatory-bound]
  4348	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4349	  status: reusable
  4350	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-masked-trig-products-bridged-paper
  4351	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.masked_trig_products_bridged_paper
  4352	  kind: theorem
  4353	  summary: "With the hypotheses of masked_trig_products_paper, but hnorm (|emb f|^2 = Re timeForm a T f f for f in V with f in L^2(0,T)) in place of hmod; hmem (modes in V, emb linear) kept: 1_I A P_r Q_rho is in V and |emb(it)|^2 <= C0(a) h^(2-a) (M+hD)^2 Q_h(r,rho)."
  4354	  keywords: [trigonometric-product, norm-identity]
  4355	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4356	  status: reusable
  4357	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr
  4358	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr
  4359	  kind: definition
  4360	  summary: "acorr Phi v = int_R Phi(u+v) conj(Phi u) du (Bochner; Lean's 0 if not integrable). For Phi = 1_I A and 0 <= v <= h it is the c(v) of the proof of L:masked-temporal-modulation."
  4361	  keywords: [autocorrelation, temporal-modulation]
  4362	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4363	  status: reusable
  4364	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-bound
  4365	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_bound
  4366	  kind: theorem
  4367	  summary: "If Phi = 0 outside [s,s+h] and |Phi u| <= M for all u: for every real v, |acorr Phi v| <= M*M*max(h - v, 0)."
  4368	  keywords: [autocorrelation, envelope-bound]
  4369	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4370	  status: reusable
  4371	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-lip
  4372	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_lip
  4373	  kind: theorem
  4374	  summary: "If Phi measurable, = 0 outside I=[s,s+h], |Phi| <= M, |Phi x - Phi y| <= D|x-y| on I, h >= 0, D >= 0, 0 <= v <= w: |acorr Phi v - acorr Phi w| <= (M*M + h*M*D)(w - v)."
  4375	  keywords: [autocorrelation, lipschitz-bound]
  4376	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4377	  status: reusable
  4378	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-neg
  4379	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_neg
  4380	  kind: theorem
  4381	  summary: "For every Phi : R -> C and real v: acorr Phi (-v) = conj(acorr Phi v)."
  4382	  keywords: [autocorrelation, conjugate-symmetry]
  4383	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4384	  status: reusable
  4385	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-time-form-eq-acorr
  4386	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.timeForm_eq_acorr
  4387	  kind: theorem
  4388	  summary: "If a < 1, Phi measurable, = 0 outside I=[s,s+h], |Phi| <= M, h >= 0, I in [0,T]: with F = Phi * e^(i omega .), timeForm a T F F = int_R |v|^(-a) e^(i omega v) acorr Phi v dv."
  4389	  keywords: [convolution-form, fubini]
  4390	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4391	  status: reusable
  4392	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-integral-acorr-split
  4393	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.integral_acorr_split
  4394	  kind: theorem
  4395	  summary: "If a < 1, Phi measurable, = 0 outside [s,s+h], |Phi| <= M, h >= 0: int_R |v|^(-a) e^(i omega v) acorr Phi v dv = X + conj X with X the same integral over v > 0."
  4396	  keywords: [conjugate-symmetry, temporal-modulation]
  4397	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4398	  status: reusable
  4399	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-crude-bound
  4400	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.crude_bound
  4401	  kind: theorem
  4402	  summary: "If a < 1, h > 0, B >= 0, C : R -> C with |C v| <= B max(h - v, 0) for v >= 0: for every omega, |int_(v>0) v^(-a) e^(i omega v) C(v) dv| <= B h h^(1-a)/(1-a)."
  4403	  keywords: [oscillatory-integral, crude-bound]
  4404	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4405	  status: reusable
  4406	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-osc-bound
  4407	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.osc_bound
  4408	  kind: theorem
  4409	  summary: "If 0<a<1, 0<delta<h, B,L>=0, C a.e.-measurable, |C v| <= B max(h-v,0) (v>=0), |C v - C w| <= L(w-v) (0<=v<=w<=h), e^(i omega delta) = -1: |int_(v>0) v^(-a) e^(i omega v) C v| <= (2hB delta^(1-a) + (L+B) delta h^(1-a))/(2(1-a))."
  4410	  keywords: [oscillatory-integral, half-period-shift]
  4411	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4412	  status: reusable
  4413	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-envelope-of-cont-diff-on
  4414	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.envelope_of_contDiffOn
  4415	  kind: theorem

4416	  summary: "If h > 0, A C^1 on I=[s,s+h] (ContDiffOn R 1), M = sSup of |A| over I, D = sSup of |derivWithin A I| over I: A is continuous on I, |A| <= M on I, and |A x - A y| <= D|x - y| for x, y in I."
  4417	  keywords: [c1-envelope, mean-value]
  4418	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4419	  status: reusable
  4420	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-mem-lp-mode-fn
  4421	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.memLp_modeFn
  4422	  kind: theorem
  4423	  summary: "If A is continuous on I=[s,s+h] with |A| <= M on I: for every T and real omega, modeFn I A omega = 1_I A e^(i omega t) is in L^2(0,T) (MemLp 2 on [0,T])."
  4424	  keywords: [l2-membership, modulated-amplitude]
  4425	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4426	  status: reusable
  4427	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-profile-sub-le
  4428	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.profile_sub_le
  4429	  kind: theorem
  4430	  summary: "If 0<a, 0<delta<h, B,L>=0, |C v| <= B max(h-v,0) (v>=0), |C v - C w| <= L(w-v) (0<=v<=w<=h): for every v, |profile a C v - profile a C (v+delta)| <= majorant a h B L delta v."
  4431	  keywords: [half-period-shift, majorant]
  4432	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4433	  status: internal
  4434	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-majorant-integrable
  4435	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.majorant_integrable
  4436	  kind: theorem
  4437	  summary: "If a < 1 and 0 < delta < h: majorant a h B L delta is integrable on R (any B, L)."
  4438	  keywords: [majorant, integrability]
  4439	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4440	  status: internal
  4441	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-majorant-integral-le
  4442	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.majorant_integral_le
  4443	  kind: theorem
  4444	  summary: "If a < 1, 0 < delta < h, B >= 0, L >= 0: int_R majorant a h B L delta <= (2 h B delta^(1-a) + (L+B) delta h^(1-a))/(1-a)."
  4445	  keywords: [majorant, rpow-integral]
  4446	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4447	  status: internal
  4448	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-constant-small
  4449	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.constant_small
  4450	  kind: theorem
  4451	  summary: "If 0<a<1, h>0, B <= K^2 and <x> <= 8: 2 B h^(2-a) <= 16 h^(2-a) K^2 <x>^(a-1)."
  4452	  keywords: [constant-check, bracket]
  4453	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4454	  status: internal
  4455	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-constant-large
  4456	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.constant_large
  4457	  kind: theorem
  4458	  summary: "If 0<a<1, h>0, k>7, B <= K^2, L+B <= 2K^2: 2hB(pi h/k)^(1-a) + (L+B)(pi h/k)h^(1-a) <= 16 h^(2-a) K^2 <k>^(a-1) (4 pi 8/7 <= 16 replaces the TeX's 8 sqrt2 <= 16)."
  4459	  keywords: [constant-check, bracket]
  4460	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4461	  status: internal
  4462	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-shear-integrable
  4463	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.shear_integrable
  4464	  kind: theorem
  4465	  summary: "If a<1, Phi measurable, = 0 outside [s,s+h], |Phi| <= M, h >= 0: (t,v) -> F t conj(F(t-v)) |v|^(-a), F = Phi e^(i omega .), is integrable on R^2."
  4466	  keywords: [fubini, integrability]
  4467	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4468	  status: internal
  4469	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-integrable
  4470	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_integrable
  4471	  kind: theorem
  4472	  summary: "If Phi measurable, = 0 outside [s,s+h], |Phi| <= M: for every v, u -> Phi(u+v) conj(Phi u) is integrable on R."
  4473	  keywords: [autocorrelation, integrability]
  4474	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4475	  status: internal
  4476	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-integrand-le
  4477	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_integrand_le
  4478	  kind: theorem
  4479	  summary: "If Phi = 0 outside [s,s+h] and |Phi| <= M: for all v, u, |Phi(u+v) conj(Phi u)| <= indicator of [s, s+h-v] of M*M at u."
  4480	  keywords: [autocorrelation, pointwise-bound]
  4481	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4482	  status: internal
  4483	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-bound-abs
  4484	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.acorr_bound_abs
  4485	  kind: theorem
  4486	  summary: "If Phi = 0 outside [s,s+h] and |Phi| <= M: for every real v, |acorr Phi v| <= M*M*max(h - |v|, 0)."
  4487	  keywords: [autocorrelation, envelope-bound]
  4488	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4489	  status: internal
  4490	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-acorr-strongly-measurable

  4492	  kind: theorem
  4493	  summary: "If Phi is measurable: acorr Phi is strongly measurable."
  4494	  keywords: [autocorrelation, measurability]
  4495	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4496	  status: internal
  4497	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-m-nonneg-of-bound
  4498	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.M_nonneg_of_bound
  4499	  kind: theorem
  4500	  summary: "If |Phi u| <= M for all u: 0 <= M."

  4503	  status: internal
  4504	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-integrable-kern-indicator

  4511	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-mode-fn-eq-indicator-mul
  4512	  decl: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.MaskedModulation.modeFn_eq_indicator_mul

  4518	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-ii-rpow-shift

  4520	  kind: theorem

  4525	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-integral-rpow-shift

  4530	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
  4531	  status: internal
  4532	- id: stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean/masked-modulation-integrable-indicator-ioc

  4544	  file: StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/MaskedModulation.lean
